0778f334fcb6: Salesforce Gantt Chart: No-Code Project Plans on Any Object
785eb85ebe0f: The MultiDatePick Gantt view for Salesforce: projects, phases and tasks from any object on one chart, with project health, milestones, percent done, task links with types and lag, drag that moves waiting tasks, critical path with slack and planned dates as a baseline. Set up in the Setup Wizard with no code.
840e3221c334: A Salesforce Gantt chart on any object, set up with no code: projects, phases and milestones, linked tasks that move together, critical path and baseline.
9be3357befe8: Is there a Gantt chart for Salesforce?
d3d135e76eb9: Yes. MultiDatePick adds a Gantt view to any Salesforce object with a start date and an end date, set up in a wizard with no code. Tasks group into phases and projects with health and milestones, links move the waiting tasks when one slips, and a critical path, slack and planned dates show what can still slip and what cannot.
a56513f2377b: How do I create a Gantt chart in Salesforce without code?
04cdf371494c: Open the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard, choose the object that holds your tasks and its start and end date fields, and tick Offer the Gantt view on the Views step. Add the calendar to a Lightning page and paste the Config Name. Phases, projects, percent done, milestones, links and planned dates are optional fields you add when you want them.
70d279d71e82: Can a Salesforce Gantt chart show task dependencies?
5a0333329cf8: Yes. Link tasks with a Waits on lookup, or with your own link object when a task waits on several others. Each link can be after it ends, when it starts or when it ends, with a lag in working days. Drag a task and every task that waits on it moves too, and one Undo puts them all back.
e8723d26d761: Does the Gantt view show the critical path?
19e0072cf905: Yes. The Critical path button highlights the tasks with no slack, where any delay moves the finish date. Each linked task's hover card says how many workdays it can slip, and a Slack column can list it for every task.
bd65fbff4565: Can I compare planned dates with actual dates in a Salesforce Gantt chart?
910f327b4799: Yes. Choose two date fields for the planned start and end. Each bar gets a plan bar under it and shows +N days when it slipped, each project shows how many days it is behind plan, and Set baseline saves the current dates as the plan.
82e75616fe6e: Which Salesforce objects can the Gantt view use?
87f49d567f24: Any standard or custom object with a date field for the start and one for the end, such as your own Project Task object. Phases and projects come from fields on the same records (a picklist, a text field or a lookup), and links come from a lookup or your own link object.
e03b0a6e4b50: Does the Gantt view skip weekends and holidays?
983fce353b47: Yes. Skip weekends is on by default, so pushes, lag and day counts skip Saturday and Sunday. Office closures from Blocked Dates and the days a resource is closed are skipped too. Turn Skip weekends off when every day is a working day.
990d5fb8a240: How many tasks can the Gantt view handle?
949eb17528d4: Hundreds. It was measured with 511 tasks and 474 links: the first draw took about 160 milliseconds, and a sort, a collapse or a new horizon about a tenth of a second, because a long chart draws only the rows near the screen.
c60bb11a60b2: Does the Gantt view cost extra?
e85a40e8254c: No. It is part of MultiDatePick, $20 per user per month with every feature in one plan and a 30-day free trial. The Gantt view is one of the calendar's views, turned on per page in the Setup Wizard.
